what: time to first streamed token, granite4.1:3b via Ollama 0.33.3 /v1
why: B5 claims live output. The claim is true and insufficient: streaming removes the wait DURING generation, not the wait before it, and on this hardware the second dominates a short turn.
method: one warm model, two calls differing only in max_output_tokens, timestamps taken in the on_chunk callback
finding: time to first token is roughly FIXED at ~2.4s and does not scale with output length, so it is prompt evaluation rather than generation. The streaming window grows with output (1.0s -> 1.4s) while the silent head does not shrink.
consequence: a surface that reacts only to tokens shows nothing for 63-71% of a short turn. The loop now publishes a `waiting` event before the model call and the TUI spins the theme's frames until the first token.
caveat: one model, one machine, warm. A cold load put first-token at 7.1s of an 8.0s call in an earlier measurement, so the silent fraction is worse on a cold tier, not better.
